notes:
# 150_scan087 — reader B

The sheet has the author’s dark page number **40** at upper left, formula numbers **(75)–(79)** at the left of their respective displays, and a thin later-hand foliation **86** at lower left. The right-hand note to (76) contains a second written reference **(77)**. No date or title is written. This is a handwritten mathematical note with one actual three-object diagram, not a typescript or a pictorial drawing.

## Content and the author’s qualifications

Formula (75) writes T for the pair of Sigma indices as an intersection with a union of T_j. Its parenthetical second expression has a cancelled pre-index character and a live barred capital whose centered stem favors I over J; both witnesses give J, but the retracing leaves that capital open. The author’s three-line note, “mais en général c’est différent…” with exactly three terminal dots, is attached by a descending leader to the parenthetical equals sign. The note is retained as an authorial caveat, not converted into an editorial mathematical correction.

Formula (76) gives a boundary expression as a directed limit of the parenthesized Sigma_d. Its three condition lines read d in Drap(I′), “premier terme de d est ∈ J”, and singular “dernier terme est dans I′\setminus J”. The redundant-looking “est ∈” is visibly written and stays. A following attempted expression involving Sigma_{i_0,i_1,i_2} and its lower annotations is crossed out. The candidate preserves the cap-like sign and three doubtful upward marks, including the mark immediately below the live d that neither witness transcribed explicitly. Their physical arrangement is retained rather than substituting H’s explanatory membership formulas. The main (Sigma_d) is live; the extra lower mark and attempted indexed-Sigma material belong to the cancelled draft. The right-hand parenthesis identifies a Sigma indexed by J,I′-J and says “avec la notation ci-dessous (77)”. Its written operation is a nearly horizontal minus, not a descending slash; its intended set-difference use is not a reason to normalize the glyph. Its exponent is separately and definitely crossed, with identity still doubtful.

The next line reads “On pose (pour L=I′\setminus J, rappelons-le)”. Formula (77) defines the indicated Sigma by removing an intersection with an open T, displays a square-ended inner bracket and an outer underbrace, and ends with an intersection with Sigma_L. The two upper bars over J′ are individually cancelled while the J and prime remain live. The cancelled character before the inner-union j is not fully readable and keeps C’s doubt. The diagonal NB formula has a clean **live** bar over J′, different from the two cancellations inside the display. No terminal period is visible at the end of (77) or of the NB note.

“On aura sauf erreur” explicitly qualifies (78), which gives a directed-limit description with first term in J and singular “dernier terme dans L”. No terminal period follows its Sigma_d. The recurring exponent at (77), (78), and (79) has a low bowl and crossing upper strokes: flat, natural, and the possible cancellation of either remain explicit alternatives. The recurrence does not by itself prove that the crossing strokes are a deletion.

Diagram (79) has an upper-left Sigma_{J,L} carrying that uncertain exponent, an upper-right Sigma_L, and a lower-left Sigma_J. A horizontal hooked arrow points right and has the two-line label “inclusion canonique” below it. The vertical arrow points down and has a left-hand label “induit par” followed by the small dotted-T map. The final t of induit has no extra e; the two Sigma subscripts of that small T are adjacent, with no written comma. The diagram is fully set in tikz-cd.

## Mathematical context used only to prompt visual rereading

The distinction between I and J in the second union of (75) prompted comparison with the ordinary J beneath the first union and the bilateral I forms in the NB note and limit conditions. The center-positioned stem and bilateral bars favor I, but the lower-bar retracing leaves a narrow I/J doubt. No set-theoretic expectation was used to replace the written capital. The whole (75) formula was read with the doubtful index.

The cancelled expression in (76) prompted a reread of the whole limit formula and of the separate annotation targets. The enlarged ink supplies three marks at distinct positions, not H’s literal strings of membership conditions. The singular condition words were checked in their own crop. The right-hand minus was compared with the distinctly oblique set-difference stroke in the nearby cancelled annotation; the horizontal glyph is preserved.

The repeated exponents and barred indices prompted whole-formula rereading of (77), (78), and the complete diagram (79). Dense bar cancellations in (77) were distinguished from the live clean bar in the NB note. The filled dots over the boundary T forms were distinguished from the open rings over interior T forms. The limit strokes in (76) and (78) were inspected at both ends: (76) has a distinct right-facing triangular head, and (78) a small connected right-facing tip. The diagram’s horizontal hook, right arrowhead, downward arrowhead, and small map arrow are visible. These are visual readings; no proof of the formulas or their compatibility has been performed.

The ordinary agreed prose, all displayed letters, primes and indices, the inner bracket and outer underbrace, all handwritten numbers, accents, punctuation, cancellations, margins and the arrow labels were read against both witnesses on the native overlapping halves. Every crop in the manifest was personally opened. The ink-favored change of first reading from barred J to barred I in (75) is logged at medium confidence with barred J retained as an alternative. Adding identity uncertainty to the right-note exponent alone is not counted as a correction to C. Unresolved C/H disagreements about the recurring exponent state are preserved with full evidence in doubts and diff coverage; broadening uncertainty alone is not counted as a reading change. The check-event list is empty because this task performed transcription and visual comparison, not proof verification.

### Blind reading corrections

The small note attached to (75) includes a detached dash after général. The separately canceled superscript in the right-hand note to (76) is a multi-character I-prime–J expression, with its separator still uncertain; it is not adequately represented by a single flat. The three lower signs in the discarded construction of (76) remain uncertain between upward arrows and quarter-turned membership signs. The inner annotation in (77) has a square-ended bracket, whereas the larger outer annotation is a cusp brace. The tiny raised T decoration in the vertical label of (79) is now marked star/dot; the adjacent Sigma subscripts still have no separating comma. The recurring Sigma exponent in77–79 remains unresolved as to both glyph and cancellation state. No new proof is claimed.
